No .mn changed; tree green at census 0. This banks the measurement that names

Publishing the decl's CELL now gets all the way through inference and emit —
m2 clean, m3 exit 0 at 532,547 lines, census 0 — and emits WAT that does not
assemble: "type mismatch in f64.load, expected [i32] but got [f64]", at
`(call $number_from_substring) (f64.load)`. The caller unboxes a result the
callee returned wide. Caller and callee disagree about the f64 ABI.

The root is in the emit's own comment: an untwinned callee emits per its
DECLARED scheme, and the wide-ref/wide-deref pair is applied "per THE ONE
SIGNATURE BOTH SIDES AGREE ON". An ABI is a contract and a contract is a fixed
fact. A live cell is time-varying, so that one signature stops existing — the
callee's body and the call site can read the decl at different moments and
choose different widths. Frozen publication did not make this correct, it made
it coincidentally agreed.

The answer is not to keep the snapshot. The legitimate settling point is not
the decl's exit — where generalize freezes today, when the cell is least
finished — it is the infer->lower/emit phase boundary, which graph_bind_row's
comment already names as "the freeze that makes lattice reads sound". Reading
a settled fact after inference completes is a read, not a snapshot. So the ABI
must be read once at that boundary instead of baked per-decl during lower:
Hb.lower.lowering-is-a-column (§11 5.5), the lower-time-bake family. Rung 3's
live cells are DEP-gated on that deletion, and this miscompile is the evidence.

mentl/1fffbbf:
The checker unconditionally returned TString for every `++` expression,
forcing `a ++ b` to be inferred as a String regardless of operand types.
The Rust VM didn't care because OpCode::Concat dispatches on runtime
types, but the self-hosted WASM compiler uses the inferred types to
pick between str_concat and list_concat. Polymorphic functions like
string_union ended up with `a : String` when `a` was actually a list,
and the WASM-compiled code called str_concat on list data, copying
bytes instead of i32 slots and corrupting every pointer in the list.

Fix: treat Concat like arithmetic. Unify operands, resolve, commit
only when a side is concretely TString or TList. If both are TVars,
return the unified tvar so a later unification can resolve it.

Supporting fixes committed alongside:
- lower_closure.lux: collect_free_match_arms_at extracts pattern-bound
  names via extract_pat_names_safe so pattern variables don't become
  false-positive captures. Earlier worry that extract_pat_names_safe
  crashed turned out to be a different bug; it works correctly here.
- wasm_emit.lux: removed instrumentation/sanity checks added during
  debugging. The vstack bump to 1 MB stays (deeply nested expressions
  in the self-hosted compiler can overflow the old 4 KB).

Status:
- All crucibles pass (hello, ultimate fib=55, counter, check env=21)
- WASM bootstrap (std/backend -> WAT via Rust VM) produces 127K valid
  lines that wasmtime compiles cleanly
- **The WASM-compiled compiler compiles Lux programs**: feeding

This is the first time the self-hosted compiler has actually executed
